questions.note: Order reads right: hallux longest, toe 2 a little shorter, 3-5 descending (V1f, V3, V4), and the pulps bulge. But toe 5 sits beside toe 4 with a gap and its nail up, not rolled and tucked under it, and toes 2-5 are smooth look-alike tubes: soft knuckles, little DIP, only faint wrinkles, no redness over the joints.

Five plates with visible free-edge thickness and a thin fold rim; none missing, floating or sunk. But the hallux nail is a glued acrylic tile: no fold or cuticle over its base, a white crescent like a lifted edge instead of a lunula, one milky tone with no bed seen through it. The lesser nails are copied tombstones with identical white French-tip edges; the 5th is not thick or ridged.

Relief exists and is placed right: a saphenous in front of the medial malleolus, an arch over the metatarsals, a fan of slips to the toes. But the veins are pale cream cords lighter than the skin, even in width, with a hairpin on the dorsum (V2), and the tendons are thin equal wires that look like the veins, the EHL no stronger than the rest.

No waxiness: toe shadow sides stay dark, the SSS is restrained and fine pores show on the hallux closeup. But the skin is uniformly smooth, clean and young, the dorsal toe skin in V5f shows little relief, the pad ridges are mechanical (one corduroy field, identical target whorls with seams) and the glossy nails read as plastic.

defects.what: The great saphenous and the dorsal arch are pale cream cords, lighter than the skin and even in width, with a sharp hairpin on the dorsum; they read as scar lines or tubing laid on the skin, not veins seen through it. The same cord runs on up the shin.
defects.fix: Foot veins are soft 3-4 mm swellings darker and cooler than the skin (blue-grey to green), varying in width and fading in and out, with a highlight only along the crest; the arch curves smoothly across the metatarsals.

defects.what: The hallux nail is a glued acrylic tile: a milky pale-pink glossy plate of one tone with a crisp outline, no proximal fold or cuticle lapping onto it, a white crescent at its base like the plate's lifted edge, and an even grey-white slab of free edge.
defects.fix: A man's big toenail is thick, satin to matte, faintly yellowed and ridged, its base under a skin fold with a cuticle, the lunula half hidden, the pink bed seen through the plate, the free edge opaque and uneven with grime beneath.

defects.what: Nails 2-5 are copies of one rounded tombstone of the same glossy pale pink with the same thin bright white free-edge line, a French manicure that reads even at native size; the 5th is a small copy, not a thick ridged nail.
defects.fix: Lesser toenails differ toe to toe: narrower, more curved, often thickened, dull and partly buried in the folds; the 5th small, thick, ridged and rough; free edges irregular and off-white, not a crisp white stripe.

defects.what: No hair on the dorsum or the instep at all, so the foot reads shaved; the only hairs are a few short strokes on the hallux and the toe bases.
defects.fix: A man's foot carries sparse dark terminal hairs, about 2 per cm2, 6-10 mm long, lying flat toward the toes and thinning out by mid-foot, plus a tuft on the hallux's proximal phalanx, as in the anchor photos.

defects.what: The extensor tendons are a row of thin, evenly spaced, wire-like ridges about 1.5-2 mm wide running at full strength down to the webs; the EHL is no stronger than the slips to toes 2-5, and tendons and veins look alike.
defects.fix: The EHL is the dominant 5 mm cord to the hallux; the slips to toes 2-5 are softer 3-4 mm cords that fan out and fade before the knuckles, read as broad low relief, not as lines.

defects.what: Toe 5 sits beside toe 4 as a separate small toe at the same level, with a gap between them and its nail facing up, instead of rolled outward and tucked partly under toe 4.
defects.fix: On a boot-wearer's foot the little toe is rolled 35-40 degrees, nail facing up and out, curled, and tucked partly under the 4th toe, touching it.

defects.what: From the medial side the arch is low: the medial border hangs only a few mm over the floor from heel to ball, no navicular tuberosity shows, and the instep is a straight ramp from the ankle crease to the toes.
defects.fix: A normal male foot lifts its medial border clearly off the floor at mid-foot, with the navicular tuberosity a small dome about 40 mm up and the instep rising to a convex crest before descending to the toes.

defects.what: Toes 2-5 are smooth tubes: soft knuckles, little DIP definition, only a few faint wrinkles over the joints and no redness over the knuckles; they read young and pedicured.
defects.fix: A forty-year-old's toes show knobbly PIP knuckles, 3-6 transverse wrinkles over each joint, ruddier skin over the knuckles and a drier, rougher surface.

defects.what: The heel callus is a grey-cream band printed with an even mesh of fine dark polygons, like crackle glaze or dried mud, under a speckled, noise-dithered top edge; a grey-green cast along its bottom reads as grime.
defects.fix: Heel callus is thick yellow-cream skin, matte and slightly translucent, with a few deeper fissures running up the rim, flaky at its margin and merging gradually into the heel skin.

defects.what: The ball and toe bases carry one uniform field of parallel wavy ridges, the same pitch, depth and direction everywhere, like corduroy, unbroken by the ball crease and not flattened by callus.
defects.fix: Plantar ridges change direction across the ball, break at creases, flatten where the skin is callused, and show only faintly at this distance under dry, varied skin.

defects.what: Each toe pad's whorl is a perfect target of concentric ovals; on the hallux (and toe 3) a straight seam runs from the IP crease into the whorl centre where the ridge phase jumps.
defects.fix: Real pad ridges form loops and whorls with bifurcations, ridge endings and pores, different on every toe, with no seams.

defects.what: Only the heel rim carries callus: none under the 1st-2nd metatarsal heads (the ball is pink and smooth), none on the lateral 5th MTP, none on the medial side of the hallux IP, and no corn on toe 4's PIP.
defects.fix: A boot-wearing soldier's foot shows paler, drier, rougher callus under the ball, at the 5th MTP's lateral border and on the medial hallux, and here a small dorsal corn on the left 4th toe.

defects.what: From the side the lateral malleolus is a broad soft swelling, with no crisp bony apex and no hollows in front of and behind it; the outside of the ankle reads padded.
defects.fix: On a lean man the lateral malleolus is a distinct knob, lower and further back than the medial one, with a hollow in front and a groove behind it toward the Achilles.

defects.what: No 5th metatarsal tuberosity: the lateral border runs smooth from the heel to the 5th MTP with no bump at mid-foot.
defects.fix: The styloid of the 5th metatarsal is a sharp bump halfway along the lateral border, about 8 mm across and 2-3 mm proud.

defects.what: The few toe hairs are short, straight, parallel dark dashes, like scratches, not fine curved hairs lying flat toward the tips.
defects.fix: Toe hairs are fine and slightly curved, varying in length and direction, lying nearly flat along the proximal phalanx.

defects.what: Seen from below, toe 3 is crossed by a ruler-straight hairline with a slight tone step and a notch where it meets the edge: a seam rather than a flexion crease.
defects.fix: A digital flexion crease is a soft fold that follows the toe's curve, deepest at the middle and fading toward the sides.

ranked: Overall the foot reads young, clean and pedicured: hairless, smooth, glossy-nailed and unworn, a mannequin's or a catalogue model's rather than a lean forty-year-old soldier's who lives in boots; the anchor feet are hairier, knobblier, drier and more mottled.

[D1] The veins are pale cream cords, lighter than the skin and even in width, with a hairpin on the dorsum (V2) and an even pale net over the dorsum (V1f); they read as scars or tubing laid on the skin. Real veins are darker and cooler than the skin, soft-edged, fading in and out.

[D2] The hallux nail is a glued acrylic tile: one milky pink tone, crisp outline, no fold or cuticle over its base, a white crescent like a lifted edge, a clean grey-white slab of free edge. A man's big toenail is thicker, duller, faintly yellow and ridged, tucked under its folds.

[D3] Nails 2-5 are one rounded tombstone copied at four sizes, each with the same thin bright white free edge, so every toe shows a French tip even at native size (V1f, V3). Real lesser nails differ toe to toe, dull and partly buried in their folds, the 5th small, thick and rough.

[D4] The dorsum and instep carry no hair at all and the toes only a few strokes, so the foot looks shaved. Men's feet, as in the anchor, carry sparse dark hairs lying flat toward the toes and a tuft on the big toe.

[D5] The extensor tendons are thin equal ridges at even spacing, like wires, running at full strength to the webs; the EHL does not lead and the tendons are hard to tell from the veins. Real extensors are soft broad cords, the EHL strongest, fading before the knuckles.
[D6] Toe 5 stands beside toe 4 as a separate small toe with a gap and its nail facing up (V1f, V5f, hr.lesser), instead of rolled outward and tucked partly under the 4th as on a boot-wearer's foot.

[D7] From the medial side the arch is low and the instep a straight ramp: no navicular tuberosity, the medial border a few mm off the floor (V2). The foot reads flat; a fit man's arch lifts clearly and the instep crests before falling to the toes.

[D8] The lesser toes are smooth tubes with soft knuckles, little DIP, only faint wrinkles and no redness over the joints; they read like a young person's or a mannequin's, not knobbly toes cramped in boots for twenty years.

[D9] The heel callus is printed with an even crackle of fine dark polygons under a speckled noise edge, with a grey-green cast that reads as grime (V8). Real heel callus is thick, yellowish and matte, with a few deeper rim fissures and a gradual, flaky margin.

[D10] The ball and toe bases are one uniform field of parallel wavy ridges, like corduroy, the same pitch and direction everywhere (hr.plantar); real plantar ridges change direction, break at creases and flatten under callus.
[D11] Every toe pad carries the same perfect target of concentric ovals, and the hallux and toe 3 have a straight seam running into the whorl centre where the ridges jump.

[D12] Only the heel rim is callused: the ball under the 1st-2nd metatarsal heads is pink and smooth, and the lateral 5th MTP callus, the medial hallux pinch callus and toe 4's dorsal corn are all missing.
[D13] The lateral malleolus is a soft broad swelling with no bony apex and no hollows around it (V3); the outside of the ankle reads padded rather than lean and bony.

Colour is still one peach tone over dorsum, ankle and toes: knuckles not reddened, toes barely pinker, no grey-green cast along the veins (which are paler than the skin instead), no trace of boot or sock wear.
[D14] No 5th metatarsal tuberosity: the lateral border runs smooth from heel to the 5th MTP with no bump at mid-foot (V3).
The front of the ankle is one smooth curve, with no anterior ankle crease and no tibialis anterior cord (V1f, V2).
[D15] The few toe hairs are short, straight, parallel dark dashes, like scratches, not fine curved hairs lying flat toward the tips (hr.lesser, V5f).
[D16] From below, toe 3 is crossed by a ruler-straight hairline with a slight tone step and a notch at its edge, reading as a seam rather than a flexion crease (hr.plantar).
